title: Hunt architecture diagram
description: One of the shape diagrams the Hunt client renders from `.hunt/diagram.<type>.json`: a C4 context or container diagram, a UML state diagram, an entity-relationship diagram or a UML activity (process) diagram. The file holds content only (elements, their connections, labels and what the session changed); Hunt owns shapes, colors, sizes and layout, so the same diagram looks the same on every branch.

type.description: Which diagram the file holds; must match the file name `diagram.<type>.json`.

title.description: What the diagram shows in a few words, e.g. the subsystem or the flow it covers.

groups.description: Boundaries that enclose the nodes naming them as `parent`, e.g. the system under review in a C4 container diagram.

change.description: What the session did to this element: `added` when the session's changes introduce it, `changed` when they alter it. Leave it out for everything the session did not touch; Hunt highlights added and changed elements against the unchanged context.

id.description: Stable kebab-case id derived from the element's name (`order-service`, `session-vm`, `awaiting-payment`), so the same element has the same id on every branch; referenced by edges and never changed when the label is reworded.

kind.description: Which shape Hunt draws. c4-context: `person`, `system` (the system under review), `externalSystem`. c4-container: `person`, `container` (a deployable process: app, service, job), `database`, `queue`, `externalSystem`. states: `start`, `end`, `state`. erd: `table`. process: `start`, `end`, `action`, `decision`.

label.description: The element's name as the team calls it; a `start` or `end` node may carry an empty-looking short label such as `Start`.

description.description: Second line under the label: a container's technology (`Node, Express`), a system's purpose, a person's role, a state's meaning, a table's purpose. Shown on the shape.

parent.description: `id` of the group the element sits in; omitted for elements outside every boundary.

actor.description: process only: who or what performs an `action` (a role, a service, a job).

columns.description: erd only, required for a `table`: its columns in the order they are declared.

name.description: Column name as declared; edges reference it in `sourceColumn` and `targetColumn`.

type.description: Column type as declared (`uuid`, `text`, `timestamptz`, an enum name).

id.description: Stable kebab-case id, referenced by the `parent` of its nodes.

label.description: Name of the boundary, e.g. the system under review.

source.description: `id` of the node the connection starts at: the caller, the state left, the step before, the table holding the foreign key.

target.description: `id` of the node the connection ends at: the callee, the state entered, the next step, the table holding the referenced key.

label.description: One to four words on the connection. c4: how source uses target (`reads orders`, `sends events over HTTPS`). states: the event that triggers the transition (`payment received`). process: the answer on an edge leaving a `decision` (yes/no in the diagram's language), otherwise empty. erd: the relationship as a verb (`belongs to`).

description.description: One to three sentences on what the connection carries and why; shown when the edge is hovered.

sourceColumn.description: erd only: the column of `source` that holds the foreign key.

targetColumn.description: erd only: the column of `target` it references, usually the primary key.

source.description: How many `source` rows take part: `many` for the foreign-key side of a one-to-many relationship.

target.description: How many `target` rows take part: `one` for the referenced primary key.

cardinality.description: erd only: crow's-foot ends of the relationship.
